compound.name: estragole (methyl chavicol)
compound.one_liner: Aniseed-scented basil constituent; a genotoxic carcinogen in rodents with an EMA exposure guidance value.

occurrences.source_citation: Muráriková A, Ťažký A, Neugebauerová J, et al. (2017) Characterization of essential oil composition in different basil species and pot cultures by a GC-MS method. Molecules 22(7):1221
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: ESTRAGOLE Leaf Essent. Oil 7500-900000 ppm (0.75-90 % of oil); Plant 35-9000 ppm; METHYL-CHAVICOL Plant 238-8780 ppm. Paper: estragole a main compound only in 'Lettuce Leaf' (2.27 mg/mL); strongly chemotype-dependent. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %)

pharmacology.primary_targets: No pharmacological target researched; its importance here is metabolic toxicology [4].
pharmacology.mechanism: EMA describes bioactivation by 1'-hydroxylation followed by sulfoconjugation to a reactive ester that binds DNA, with hepatocellular carcinomas in rodents [4].

evidence.claim: Estragole is genotoxic and hepatocarcinogenic in rodents after metabolic activation.
evidence.outcome_summary: EMA judges the rodent evidence relevant for human risk assessment and sets a guidance value.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.detail: Chemotype-dependent in basil: from a main compound in only one of seven cultivars studied [18] up to 0.75-90 % of leaf oil in Duke's records.
safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: 0.05 mg/person/day for adults; 1.0 µg/kg bw for children up to 11 years (EMA guidance values for herbal medicinal products)
safety_flags.source_citation: EMA/HMPC public statement on estragole, EMA/HMPC/137212/2005 Rev 1 Corr 1 (2021)

compound.teaching_note: Estragole shows why a cultivar name matters: the same species can be nearly free of it or dominated by it [18]. EMA notes a possible (hypothetical) protective matrix effect of the basil flavonoid nevadensin [4].
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
Per-cultivar estragole values for the greenhouse cultivars (Thai, compact) not sourced.
